title: Life in one line
summary: Conway's Game of Life as one line of X_eTaL, taken apart: nine shifted copies of the board, their sum, one comparison. Every board is an array X_eTaL printed.

scenes.heading: Life in one line
scenes.narration: Conway's Game of Life, in a single line of code.
lines: Conway's Game of Life, in X_eTaL.
The whole rule is one line of array code.

scenes.heading: The rule
scenes.narration: Here is the whole rule. {Read|Read} it from right to left. Rotate the board, add up the copies, and compare.
lines: Read it right to left: rotate, add, compare.
No loops over cells. No neighbor bookkeeping.

scenes.heading: 1. Nine shifted copies
scenes.narration: Rotate the board by minus one, zero, and one, in both directions. That gives nine shifted copies, one for each neighbor, and one for the cell itself.
lines: One copy for each neighbor, and the cell itself.

scenes.heading: 2. Add them up
scenes.narration: Add up the nine copies. Now every cell holds its own value, plus its eight neighbors.
lines: Every cell now holds itself plus its eight neighbors.

scenes.heading: 3. Compare
scenes.narration: A cell is alive next time when the sum is three, or when it is alive now and the sum is four.
lines: Alive next: the sum is 3, or the cell is alive and the sum is 4.

scenes.heading: Run it
scenes.narration: Run it. Start with just five cells, on a sixteen by sixteen board that wraps around.
lines: Five cells to start: the R-pentomino. The edges wrap.
